title.en: Because it rained, so we stayed
title.it: Collegare le frasi: because, so, when

goal.sl: Povežeš, kar znaš povedati: and, but, or; razlog in posledica (because, so); kdaj se je kaj zgodilo (when, before, after) in kaj je bilo potem (then).
goal.de: Du verbindest, was du sagen kannst: and, but, or; Grund und Folge (because, so); wann etwas war (when, before, after) und was dann kam (then).
goal.it: Colleghi quello che sai dire: and, but, or; il motivo e il risultato (because, so); quando è successo qualcosa (when, before, after) e che cosa è venuto dopo (then).
goal.en: You can join what you say: and, but, or; the reason and the result (because, so); when something happened (when, before, after) and what came next (then).

say.sl: Tri majhne besede povezujejo: **and** (in: še nekaj), **but** (ampak: nasprotje), **or** (ali: izbira): **We had soup and bread.** (Imeli smo juho in kruh.) **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** (Jack je bil utrujen, ampak vesel.) **Tea or coffee?** (Čaj ali kavo?) Pred **but** je navadno vejica.
say.de: Drei kleine Wörter verbinden: **and** (und: noch etwas), **but** (aber: das Gegenteil), **or** (oder: eine Wahl): **We had soup and bread.** (Wir hatten Suppe und Brot.) **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** (Jack war müde, aber froh.) **Tea or coffee?** (Tee oder Kaffee?) Vor **but** steht meist ein Komma.
say.it: Tre piccole parole collegano: **and** (e: ancora qualcosa), **but** (ma: il contrario), **or** (o: una scelta): **We had soup and bread.** (Abbiamo mangiato minestra e pane.) **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** (Jack era stanco, ma contento.) **Tea or coffee?** (Tè o caffè?) Prima di **but** di solito c'è la virgola.
say.en: Three small words join things: **and** (one more), **but** (the opposite), **or** (a choice): **We had soup and bread.** **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** **Tea or coffee?** A comma usually comes before **but**.

say.sl: **because** (ker) pove razlog, **so** (zato) posledico: **We stayed at home because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed at home.** (Ostali smo doma, ker je deževalo. Deževalo je, zato smo ostali doma.) Pred **so** je vejica. Naslov lekcije imenuje obe besedi, pravi stavek pa ima samo eno: nikoli *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
say.de: **because** (weil) nennt den Grund, **so** (also) die Folge: **We stayed at home because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed at home.** (Wir blieben zu Hause, weil es regnete. Es regnete, also blieben wir zu Hause.) Vor **so** steht ein Komma. Der Titel der Lektion nennt beide Wörter, ein echter Satz hat nur eines: nie *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
say.it: **because** (perché) dà il motivo, **so** (quindi) il risultato: **We stayed at home because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed at home.** (Siamo rimasti a casa perché pioveva. Pioveva, quindi siamo rimasti a casa.) Prima di **so** c'è la virgola. Il titolo della lezione nomina tutte e due le parole, una frase vera ne ha una sola: mai *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
say.en: **because** gives the reason, **so** the result: **We stayed at home because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed at home.** A comma comes before **so**. The lesson's title names both words; a real sentence takes one: never *Because it rained, so we stayed*.

**Posledica: so**

explain.de:

explain.it:

say.sl: Na **Why?** (zakaj?) odgovoriš z **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** (Zakaj si {m:ostal|f:ostala}? — Ker je deževalo.) Stavek se lahko z njim tudi začne, z vejico za razlogom: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** (Ker je deževalo, smo ostali doma.) V govoru je **because** pogosto *cos*.
say.de: Auf **Why?** (warum?) antwortest du mit **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** (Warum bist du geblieben? — Weil es regnete.) Auch ein Satz kann damit beginnen, mit Komma nach dem Grund: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** (Weil es regnete, blieben wir zu Hause.) Das Verb steht gleich nach it, nicht am Ende. Gesprochen ist **because** oft *cos*.
say.it: A **Why?** (perché?) rispondi con **because**: l'italiano ha una parola sola, l'inglese due: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** (Perché sei rimast{m:o|f:a}? — Perché pioveva.) Anche una frase può cominciare così, con la virgola dopo il motivo: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** (Poiché pioveva, siamo rimasti a casa.) A voce **because** spesso è *cos*.
say.en: **Why?** is answered with **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** A sentence can open with it, a comma after the reason: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** Spoken, **because** is often *cos*.

say.sl: **when** (ko), **before** (preden) in **after** (potem ko) povedo, kdaj: **When I got home, it was dark.** (Ko sem {m:prišel|f:prišla} domov, je bila tema.) **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** (Preden sem {m:šel|f:šla} spat, sem zaprl{m:|f:a} vrata.) **After we ate, we washed up.** (Ko smo pojedli, smo pomili posodo.) Če je ta del na začetku, je vejica; na koncu je ni: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**
say.de: **when** (als), **before** (bevor) und **after** (nachdem) sagen, wann: **When I got home, it was dark.** (Als ich heimkam, war es dunkel.) **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** (Bevor ich schlafen ging, machte ich die Tür zu.) **After we ate, we washed up.** (Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, wuschen wir ab.) Steht dieser Teil vorn, kommt ein Komma; hinten keines: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**
say.it: **when** (quando), **before** (prima di) e **after** (dopo) dicono quando: **When I got home, it was dark.** (Quando sono arrivat{m:o|f:a} a casa, era buio.) **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** (Prima di andare a letto, ho chiuso la porta.) **After we ate, we washed up.** (Dopo aver mangiato, abbiamo lavato i piatti.) Se questa parte viene prima, c'è la virgola; dopo, no: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**
say.en: **when**, **before** and **after** say when: **When I got home, it was dark.** **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** **After we ate, we washed up.** If this part comes first, put a comma; if it comes second, none: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**

say.sl: **then** (potem) pove, kaj je bilo naslednje, korak za korakom: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** (Povečerjali smo. Potem smo šli domov.) Ali z **and**: **We had dinner and then we went home.** Za **then** ni vejice. **then** pove samo, kaj je bilo naslednje; **so** pove, zakaj.
say.de: **then** (dann) sagt, was als Nächstes kam, Schritt für Schritt: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** (Wir aßen zu Abend. Dann gingen wir heim.) Oder mit **and**: **We had dinner and then we went home.** Nach **then** kein Komma. **then** sagt nur, was als Nächstes kam; **so** sagt, warum.
say.it: **then** (poi) dice che cosa è venuto dopo, passo dopo passo: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** (Abbiamo cenato. Poi siamo andati a casa.) Oppure con **and**: **We had dinner and then we went home.** Dopo **then** niente virgola. **then** dice solo che cosa è venuto dopo; **so** dice perché.
say.en: **then** says what came next, step by step: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** Or with **and**: **We had dinner and then we went home.** No comma after **then**. **then** only says what came next; **so** says why.

say.sl: Zdaj vse skupaj, kot v pravi zgodbi: **I was cooking when Sam came in.** (Ravno sem {m:kuhal|f:kuhala}, ko je vstopil Sam.) **He was wet because it was raining, so I made him a cup of tea.** (Moker je bil, ker je deževalo, zato sem mu {m:skuhal|f:skuhala} čaj.) **We talked for an hour and then he went home.** (Pogovarjala sva se eno uro, potem je šel domov.)
say.de: Jetzt alles zusammen, wie in einer echten Geschichte: **I was cooking when Sam came in.** (Ich kochte gerade, als Sam hereinkam.) **He was wet because it was raining, so I made him a cup of tea.** (Er war nass, weil es regnete, also machte ich ihm eine Tasse Tee.) **We talked for an hour and then he went home.** (Wir redeten eine Stunde, und dann ging er heim.)
say.it: Adesso tutto insieme, come in una vera storia: **I was cooking when Sam came in.** (Stavo cucinando quando è entrato Sam.) **He was wet because it was raining, so I made him a cup of tea.** (Era bagnato perché pioveva, quindi gli ho fatto una tazza di tè.) **We talked for an hour and then he went home.** (Abbiamo parlato per un'ora e poi è andato a casa.)
say.en: Now all of it together, as in a real story: **I was cooking when Sam came in.** **He was wet because it was raining, so I made him a cup of tea.** **We talked for an hour and then he went home.**

title.it: La brutta giornata del signor Tyson

exercises.text: It was market day, ___ Mr Tyson got up at five. He had a cup of tea ___ some bread and ___ he went to the bus stop. The bus was late ___ there was snow on the road. He waited for an hour, ___ it didn't come, ___ he walked. ___ he got to Keswick, the market was closed!

explain.sl:
**Del z when na začetku: vejica**
- When he got to Keswick, the market was closed.
explain.de:
**Der Teil mit when vorn: Komma**
- When he got to Keswick, the market was closed.
explain.it:
**La parte con when all'inizio: virgola**
- When he got to Keswick, the market was closed.
explain.en:
**The when part first: a comma**
- When he got to Keswick, the market was closed.

translation.sl: Bil je tržni dan, zato je gospod Tyson vstal ob petih. Popil je skodelico čaja, pojedel nekaj kruha in potem šel na avtobusno postajo. Avtobus je zamujal, ker je bil na cesti sneg. Čakal je eno uro, ampak ni prišel, zato je šel peš. Ko je prišel v Keswick, je bila tržnica zaprta!
translation.de: Es war Markttag, also stand Mr Tyson um fünf auf. Er trank eine Tasse Tee, aß etwas Brot und ging dann zur Bushaltestelle. Der Bus hatte Verspätung, weil Schnee auf der Straße lag. Er wartete eine Stunde, aber der Bus kam nicht, also ging er zu Fuß. Als er in Keswick ankam, war der Markt geschlossen!
translation.it: Era giorno di mercato, quindi il signor Tyson si è alzato alle cinque. Ha preso una tazza di tè con un po' di pane e poi è andato alla fermata dell'autobus. L'autobus era in ritardo perché c'era neve sulla strada. Ha aspettato per un'ora, ma non è arrivato, quindi è andato a piedi. Quando è arrivato a Keswick, il mercato era chiuso!
translation.en: It was market day, so Mr Tyson got up at five. He had a cup of tea and some bread and then he went to the bus stop. The bus was late because there was snow on the road. He waited for an hour, but it didn't come, so he walked. When he got to Keswick, the market was closed!

exercises.text: I was reading ___ Sam came in. He was very wet ___ it was raining. I made him a cup of tea. "Milk ___ sugar?" I asked. There was no milk, ___ he had sugar. We talked for an hour and ___ he went home.

translation.sl: Ravno sem bral{m:|f:a}, ko je vstopil Sam. Bil je čisto moker, ker je deževalo. Skuhal{m:|f:a} sem mu čaj. »Mleko ali sladkor?« sem {m:vprašal|f:vprašala}. Mleka ni bilo, zato je vzel sladkor. Pogovarjala sva se eno uro, potem je šel domov.
translation.de: Ich las gerade, als Sam hereinkam. Er war ganz nass, weil es regnete. Ich machte ihm eine Tasse Tee. „Milch oder Zucker?“, fragte ich. Es gab keine Milch, also nahm er Zucker. Wir redeten eine Stunde, und dann ging er heim.
translation.it: Stavo leggendo quando è entrato Sam. Era tutto bagnato perché pioveva. Gli ho fatto una tazza di tè. «Latte o zucchero?» ho chiesto. Il latte non c'era, quindi ha preso lo zucchero. Abbiamo parlato per un'ora e poi è andato a casa.
translation.en: I was reading when Sam came in. He was very wet because it was raining. I made him a cup of tea. "Milk or sugar?" I asked. There was no milk, so he had sugar. We talked for an hour and then he went home.
